comment: Prices: on-demand per GPU-hour from https://www.runpod.io/pricing and https://www.runpod.io/gpu-pricing, fetched 2026-10-21 (page says 'Updated October 8, 2026'); on-demand $/GPU-hour, storage $0.10/GB/month while running. Hours: 6*N*tokens FLOPs at 25% MFU of the GPU's dense BF16 peak, at least 12 ms per step, plus 120 s per run and the setup time (download, BVH parsing, IK).
data_path: For the H2 every source goes through BVH -> 19 canonical keypoints -> batched IK on the GPU (CMU, Bandai Namco, LAFAN1, HiPHI). The two G1-native Hugging Face sets (Unitree's LAFAN1 retarget, Retargeted AMASS) are used only when PINE_ROBOT=g1.

datasets.name: CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database (BVH conversion by B. Hahne)
datasets.hours_note: kept after QA in the CPU ingest (2,333 of 2,548 takes)
datasets.license: Free to use, including in commercial products; the data itself may not be resold

datasets.name: Bandai Namco Research Motion Dataset 1 and 2
datasets.hours_note: kept after QA in the CPU ingest (169 + 2,456 takes)

datasets.name: Ubisoft La Forge Animation Dataset (LAFAN1)
datasets.hours_note: README: 77 sequences, 496,672 frames at 30 fps, 5 subjects
datasets.access: public (git clone + git LFS for lafan1/lafan1.zip)

datasets.name: HiPHI (Noitom Robotics)
datasets.hours_note: dataset card: 371.8 h body-only + 245.7 h human-object interaction, 132 performers, 215 GB. Every motion also ships a __mirror copy; build_shards.py skips those, so if the card's total counts them about half is used. The hours actually built are in stats.json.
datasets.format: BVH, 90 Hz, cm, Y-up, 55 joints (32 .tar.zst archives)
datasets.license: ModalityNet Open Research License (research, non-commercial; commercial licensing via info@modalitynet.com)
datasets.access: gated: request access on the dataset page, then run the launcher with HF_TOKEN set; skipped otherwise

datasets.name: Unitree LAFAN1_Retargeting_Dataset (G1)
datasets.hours_note: the LAFAN1 motions, retargeted by Unitree
datasets.format: CSV, 30 fps: root xyz, quaternion xyzw (column label root_joint(XYZQXQYQZQW)), 29 joints in pine.g1.JOINTS order
datasets.path: G1-native: no IK; used only when PINE_ROBOT=g1 (replaces our IK of LAFAN1)

datasets.name: Retargeted AMASS for robotics (G1, fleaven)
datasets.hours_note: AMASS is roughly 40+ h; the retargeted hours are measured at build time. Its CMU subset is skipped when the CMU BVH is present (same motions).
datasets.format: npy rows [-1,36]: root pos, quaternion xyzw, 29 joints; fps not documented: read from the file name (..._poses_<fps>_jpos.npy, as the dataset's own visualize.py does), else 30 fps assumed and logged
datasets.license: tagged CC BY 4.0; the card says each AMASS sub-dataset's own licence applies
datasets.path: G1-native: no IK; used only when PINE_ROBOT=g1

sweep.steps: 20 epochs of the full training set, clamped to [4000, 40000]; same for every run
sweep.masking: 50% full, 30% EXO (legs + IMU only), 20% random channel groups
sweep.precision: bf16 autocast, fp32 weights; evaluation in fp32
sweep.order: model ladder -> pre-registered prediction (timestamped) -> predicted run -> data ladder

cost_guard: PINE_MAX_GPU_HOURS (default 8): before each run the sweep estimates its length from the measured tokens/s and does not start it if the GPU-hours used since the pod started would exceed the cap; every run also gets a hard deadline. The pod stops itself PINE_AUTOSTOP_MIN minutes after finishing (terminates instead if the results were already fetched).

parity.dtype: float64 on CPU (plus an fp32 check on the GPU)
compares: one AdamW step (decoupled weight decay on 2-D params except pos, clip 1.0, bias-corrected, b1 0.9, b2 0.95)
parity.gate: run_all.sh stops before any download or training if it fails
parity.status: not run yet: torch is not installed where this package was written; it runs first on the pod
parity.ik_check: gpu/retarget_torch.py vs pine/g1.py on 2,000 frames: mean keypoint difference must be < 1 mm, otherwise build_shards.py uses the NumPy solver on all CPU cores

cpu_baseline.note: CPU NumPy sweep in this repo (CMU + Bandai Namco, 900 steps x 64 windows). The GPU sweep uses more data, so its losses are on a different validation set and are not directly comparable.
